title: Air India's A350 Business Class Dazzles Even on Short Domestic Hops
excerpt: With lie-flat suites, privacy doors, and authentic Indian meals, the airline's flagship cabin turns two-hour flights into premium experiences that rival the world's best.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Air India's A350-900 features 28 lie-flat suites, rivaling top airlines like Emirates and Qatar Airways.
  • Reviewers praise the A350's business class meals as among the best for short-haul flights globally.
  • The Tata Group's overhaul includes a historic 570-aircraft order and new luxury lounges.
  • Award rates for the Maharaja Club were reduced by 25% in April 2026, enhancing value for travelers.

Air India's Airbus A350-900 has turned heads on long-haul routes to London and New York since it entered the fleet. What has surprised aviation reviewers even more is what the aircraft delivers on short domestic hops — flights of barely two hours where most airlines would never deploy their flagship cabin.

A Suite Designed for a Different Airline

The six A350s currently flying under the Air India banner were originally built for Aeroflot. Sanctions prevented their delivery, and Air India stepped in, lightly refurbishing the interiors to match its own branding while inheriting a hard product that few airlines offer on domestic routes.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=AsF55cVjzX4

The business class cabin seats 28 passengers in a staggered 1-2-1 layout using the Collins Aerospace Horizon product. Every seat has direct aisle access, fully closing privacy doors that sit noticeably higher than competitors like British Airways' Club Suite, and a bed that stretches to 6 feet 6 inches when fully flat. Storage includes a wardrobe, a deep cupboard, and a vanity cabinet with a mirror.

"The overall seat comfort is among the best in the sky. I prefer this over the Singapore Airlines Business Class seat I flew 17 hours on from Seattle."

— Grab A Mile, aviation reviewer

The in-flight entertainment system runs on a 21-inch screen with a solid selection of Bollywood and Hollywood content, and the A350 tail camera remains a favorite among aviation enthusiasts. Wi-Fi is currently free with no data caps, a rarity in business class at any price point.

Indian Food That Stands Out at 35,000 Feet

Dining has emerged as one of the A350 experience's strongest selling points. On domestic flights, passengers have reported dishes including rajma, aloo gobhi with rice, hot aloo parathas wrapped in foil, and desserts like vegan Mysore Pak and gulab jamun — all freshly plated in the galley rather than reheated in the dish.

"This was easily one of the best domestic business class meals I've had in the air in recent times," one reviewer wrote of a Hyderabad-to-Delhi flight, according to Grab A Mile. On long-haul routes, the spread expands to include chicken tikka, lamb kundan kaliyan, a Laurent-Perrier Champagne pour, and proper masala chai.

The Bigger Transformation Behind the Cabin

The A350 is just one element of Air India's overhaul under Tata Group ownership. Since the 2022 acquisition, the airline has placed a 570-aircraft order — the largest in commercial aviation history — and is systematically replacing its fleet. Air India took delivery of its first factory-built Boeing 787-9 in January 2026, with the first A350-1000 expected later this year.

On the ground, the airline opened a new 16,000-square-foot Maharaja Lounge at Delhi's Terminal 3 in February 2026, featuring a speakeasy-style cocktail bar, a quiet study, and recliners, with capacity for 300 guests. A second flagship lounge opened in San Francisco. At airports like London Heathrow where Air India lacks its own lounge, business class passengers use Singapore Airlines' SilverKris Lounge through Star Alliance.

Value for Points Travelers

Air India's Transformation

›New 16,000 sq ft Maharaja Lounge opened in Delhi.
›First A350-1000 expected later this year.
›Singapore Airlines' influence improves service quality.

Air India cut its Maharaja Club award rates by roughly 25% across international routes in April 2026, with US redemptions starting around 40,000 points. Through Air Canada's Aeroplan program, which transfers 1:1 from American Express, Chase, Capital One, and Bilt, business class awards to India run between 90,000 and 110,000 points one way with no fuel surcharges.

Singapore Airlines, which holds a 25% stake in Air India, has deepened its operational role, and the influence shows in service consistency and soft product quality, according to multiple reviewers. Whether the A350 draws a two-hour domestic hop or an eight-hour international crossing, the cabin now delivers a product that would have been unthinkable for Air India just four years ago.
